BDJ3.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 90 km away; by road, Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri on NH 110. The toy train starts at New Jalpaiguri.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Bagdogra Airport , located 90 km (56 mi) from Darjeeling.
Darjeeling can be reached by motorized vehicles on National Highway 110, from Siliguri, 77 km (48 mi) away.

BDJ4.claim: About 80% of Darjeeling's rain falls from June to September, when landslides often disrupt road and rail links.

evidence.quote: Eighty percent of the annual rainfall takes place between the months of June and September
However, road and railway communications often get disrupted in the monsoons because of landslides.

BDJ5.claim: October to November offers the clearest mountain views; April to June is also pleasant.

evidence.quote: October to November offers the clearest views
The best time to visit Observatory Hill is from April to June, when the weather is pleasant and clear for panoramic views of the mountains and Darjeeling.

BDJ6.claim: Try momos, thukpa, sha phaley, sel roti and butter tea — Darjeeling's food blends Nepali, Sikkimese, Tibetan and Bengali traditions.

evidence.quote: the culinary cultures that rule Darjeeling are varied, ranging from Nepali and Sikkimese to Tibetan and of course, Bengali.
Savour the sweet delights of Sel Roti, deep-fried rice doughnuts served with butter or chutney
And don't miss the hearty Thukpa, a hot noodle soup brimming with meat, vegetables, and spices

BDJ9.claim: The Darjeeling Carnival runs for 10 days in November, Losar (Tibetan New Year) falls in February–March, and Buddha Jayanti in May.

evidence.quote: the 10-day Darjeeling Carnival in November
In February and March, the vibrant Tibetan New Year, Losha
Finally, in May, Buddha Jayanti finds Buddhist temples adorned in celebration

BDH2.claim: Built between 1879 and 1881, the 2-ft-gauge line runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling, climbing from about 100 m to 2,200 m with six zig-zags and three loops.

evidence.quote: Built between 1879 and 1881, it is about 88 km (55 mi) long.
It climbs from about 100 m (330 ft) above sea level at New Jalpaiguri to about 2,200 m (7,200 ft) at Darjeeling, using six zig zags and three loops (originally five) to gain altitude.

BDH3.claim: Ghum station sits at 2,260 m; at Batasia Loop (1919), 5 km from Darjeeling, the track spirals around a hill beside the Gorkha War Memorial.

evidence.quote: Ghum station is situated at an altitude of 2,260 metres (7,410 ft) .
At this point, the track spirals around over itself from the bottom of a small hill and over the hilltop. It was commissioned in 1919.
It is 5 km (3 mi) from Darjeeling, below Ghum .

BTH4.claim: Everest and Kanchenjunga, both visible from Tiger Hill, are 172 km apart; the hilltop gives a 360-degree panorama.

evidence.quote: The distance between them—172 kilometres (107 miles)—adds to Everest’s mystique.
Tiger Hill provides a 360-degree panorama that stretches from the snow-capped Himalayas to the lush green valleys below.

BSD2.claim: Treks start at Manebhanjan, about 28 km (roughly an hour by road) from Darjeeling, and pass through Singalila National Park in stages via Chitre and Meghma.

evidence.quote: Treks begin at Manebhanjan which is 28 km (17 mi) (approx. 1 hour by road) from Darjeeling .
The Sandakphu trekking routes inside the Singalila National Park have four legs or stages.
Manebhanjan to Meghma – height 2,600 m (8,500 ft) : This is a 4-hour trek through the lower forest. The route goes via Chitre.

BTH1.claim: Tiger Hill (2,590 m) is famous for sunrise views of Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, with Everest visible beyond.

evidence.quote: at an elevation of 8,482 feet (2,590 meters) offers an unparalleled view of the world’s highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Mount Kanchenjunga.
Kanchenjunga, the world’s third-highest peak, dominates the scene.

BTH2.claim: In peak season crowds and traffic jams are common; Incredible India suggests arriving around 3:30 am.

evidence.quote: in peak season, there is always a throng of people making their way up – and traffic jams are not uncommon. Arrive early, around 3:30 am, to secure a spot.

BTH3.claim: Stop at Batasia Loop, Ghum Monastery and the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary on the way down.

evidence.quote: On the way back from Tiger Hill, you can stop by Batasia Loop, Ghum Monastery and the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary.

BZO2.claim: Incredible India lists 8:30 am–4:30 pm in summer and 8:30 am–4 pm in winter.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:30 AM to 04:30 PM (Summers)
08:30 AM to 04:00 PM (Winters)

BDJ10.claim: The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, founded in 1954 after the first ascent of Everest, has a museum of expedition gear and photographs, with Tenzing Norgay's memorial outside.

evidence.quote: was established in Darjeeling , India on 4 November 1954
The institute has exhibits of equipment, photographs and stories about Edmund Hillary, Tenzing Norgay and various other mountaineers.
Just outside the museum is the statue of Tenzing Norgay where his remains are also kept.

BHV3.claim: Incredible India lists opening hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 04:30 PM

BHV2.claim: Visitors can see leaves withered, rolled, oxidised and dried in the factory, then taste first- and second-flush teas.

evidence.quote: Observe how the tea leaves are dried, oxidised, rolled, and withered
from delicate first-flush brews to strong second-flush brews

BDJ11.claim: The Tibetan Refugee Self Help Centre, founded in 1959, has workshops where you can watch carpets and thangkas being made.

evidence.quote: Founded in 1959, this centre honours the courage of the Tibetan people who fled to India during political unrest.
Watch as skilled craftsmen and women create beautiful handcrafted items such as carpets, thangka paintings, and traditional Tibetan handicrafts.

BDJ12.claim: Monasteries include Yiga Choling (built 1850) at Ghum; the white Japanese Peace Pagoda was built by Nipponzan Myohoji.

evidence.quote: Yiga Choling gompa, one of the oldest monasteries in this region built in 1850
Built by the Japanese Buddhist Nipponzan Myohoji organization, the large white pagoda has numerous carvings of Buddha and his preaching.

BOB1.claim: Observatory Hill, above Chowrasta, has the Mahakal Temple and views of Kanchenjunga on clear days.

evidence.quote: Perched atop Observatory Hill, the Mahakal Temple stands as a beacon of spiritual devotion.
Rising above Chowrasta square or the Mall as it is popularly known in Darjeeling, Observatory Hill is an elevated vantage point that offers breathtaking views of snow-clad peaks

BDJ13.claim: The Mall and Chowrasta are the town's social heart — best in the evening.

evidence.quote: An ideal time to explore the famous mall road of Darjeeling is in the evening.

DJN1.claim: Tibetan handicrafts on sale include thangka paintings, engraved copper plates, singing bowls, prayer wheels and Bhutia blankets; the Gorkha khukuri knife is a classic souvenir.

evidence.quote: From exquisite Thangka paintings to intricately engraved copper plates
the Khukuri makes for a meaningful and authentic souvenir

DJN2.claim: Shop at Hong Kong Market, Batasia Loop Market, Teesta Market, Chowk Bazar and along the Mall.

evidence.quote: Whether you hunt for bargains at Hong Kong Market or Batasia Loop Market
Don't miss the iconic Mall Road, where the town comes alive.

DJN3.claim: Tea estates offer guided tours of tea-making with tastings.

evidence.quote: Embark on a guided tour of a tea estate to witness first-hand the fascinating journey of tea production.

DJN4.claim: The Teesta Tea and Tourism Festival runs in November–December and the Darjeeling Orange Festival in December.

evidence.quote: In November and December, the Teesta Tea and Tourism Festival
the unique Darjeeling Orange Festival takes centrestage

DJN5.claim: The Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Museum is in the house where he spent seven months under house arrest.

evidence.quote: this house was once the abode of Netaji, who spent seven months under house arrest here

DJN6.claim: Mark Twain rode the toy train in 1895.

evidence.quote: Mark Twain, the renowned American writer, rode this Toy Train in 1895.

DJN7.claim: Chang and thomba, fermented-grain brews, are served in bamboo mugs.

evidence.quote: Sample Chang and Thomba, local brews made from fermented grains, served in bamboo glasses

DJN8.claim: Darjeeling has no public bus system; motorised travel is by six- or eight-seat shared taxis with no fixed routes or timetables.

evidence.quote: As of 2018, Darjeeling had no public transport system of buses.
motorized travel was limited to six- or eight-seater paratransit taxis that have no set routes or timetables.

DJN9.claim: The peak tourist seasons are September–November and April–May.

evidence.quote: Darjeeling has two peak tourism seasons, September to November and April to May.

DJN10.claim: Chowrasta is the town's main gathering and shopping square.

evidence.quote: The Chowrasta is a popular shopping and gathering area

DJN11.claim: The toy train moves at about 20–25 km/h.

evidence.quote: it moves at speeds of between 20 kilometres (12 mi) and 25 kilometres (16 mi) per hour.

DJN12.claim: Landslides are a serious concern in the hills, mostly triggered by heavy rain.

evidence.quote: landslides were a serious concern in the area.
Most are triggered by excessive rainfall

DJN13.claim: Darjeeling town is at about 2,045 m.

evidence.quote: It is located at an average elevation of 2,045 m (6,709 ft)

WBF17.claim: Tiger Hill, 13 km from Darjeeling, is at 2,590 m; the Darjeeling Carnival is in November and the Orange Festival in December.

evidence.quote: Perched at an elevation of 2590 meters, just 13 kilometres from Darjeeling, lies the breath-taking Tiger Hill .
the 10-day Darjeeling Carnival in November
the unique Darjeeling Orange Festival takes centrestage

places.seoTitle: Darjeeling Travel Guide: Toy Train, Tiger Hill & Tea
places.seoDescription: Plan a Darjeeling trip: the UNESCO toy train, sunrise at Tiger Hill, Happy Valley tea estate, the zoo and HMI, monasteries, food and the best time to visit.

images.commons: File:Mount Kangchenjunga seen from Tiger Hill.jpg
images.alt: Kanchenjunga at sunrise seen from Tiger Hill

overview.text:
Darjeeling sits at about 2,045 m on a ridge in northern West Bengal, facing Kanchenjunga. The British built it as a hill station and the summer capital of the Bengal Presidency, and Tibetan refugees later added monasteries, crafts and food to its mix of Gorkha, Lepcha and Bhutia cultures.

The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO-listed toy train that Mark Twain rode in 1895, still climbs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri at 20–25 km/h, spiralling round Batasia Loop below Ghum. Sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, tea tastings on the estates, the zoo's red pandas and snow leopards, and the house where Netaji was held fill the days. Come in October–November for the clearest views, or April–May; avoid the June–September rains, when landslides cut roads.

items.title: Tea lovers

items.title: Trekkers

items.title: Festival-goers
items.body: The Darjeeling Carnival in November, the Teesta Tea and Tourism Festival in November–December and Losar in February–March.

local_transport.text: There is no public bus system. Motorised travel is by shared six- or eight-seat taxis with no fixed routes or timetables; they gather in the central bazaar. In town, walking is often quicker: Chowrasta and the Mall are the centre. Hire a taxi for the Tiger Hill sunrise trip and for Ghum and Batasia Loop, or ride the toy train there.

items.body: Darjeeling tea, straight from the estates.
Tibetan thangkas, singing bowls, prayer wheels and copper work.
A khukuri, the Gorkha knife.
Bargains at Hong Kong Market, Batasia Loop Market and Chowk Bazar; browsing on the Mall.

items.title: Landslides
items.body: Landslides are a serious concern, mostly after heavy rain. About 80% of rain falls in June–September, when roads and the railway are often disrupted. Build slack into your plans.

items.title: Cold mornings
items.body: At 2,045 m, pre-dawn Tiger Hill trips are cold. Bring warm layers.
Booking the June–September monsoon for mountain views. October–November is clearest.
Expecting buses. Shared taxis and walking are how people get around.
Riding the toy train all the way up on a tight schedule. At 20–25 km/h it is slow; the Ghum and Batasia Loop joy ride is shorter.
Skipping a tea-estate tour.

items.title: What is the best time to visit Darjeeling?
items.body: October–November for clear mountain views; April–May is the other peak season.

items.title: How do I get to Darjeeling?
items.body: Fly to Bagdogra (about 90 km) or take a train to New Jalpaiguri, then go by road (77 km from Siliguri) or the toy train.

items.title: Can I see Everest from Tiger Hill?
items.body: Yes, on clear mornings, along with Kanchenjunga.

itineraries.seoTitle: 3-Day Darjeeling Itinerary: Tiger Hill & Toy Train
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic 3-day Darjeeling plan: Tiger Hill sunrise, the toy train and Batasia Loop, Happy Valley Tea Estate, the zoo and HMI, monasteries and the Mall.

plan.overview: Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri and about 90 km from Bagdogra airport, so allow most of a day to arrive. This plan starts the morning after. Day 1 begins very early for Tiger Hill — rest in the afternoon.

prep.title: Getting there
prep.body: Bagdogra airport is about 90 km away; Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri by road, and the toy train runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri.

prep.title: Getting around
prep.body: There are no public buses; use shared or hired taxis, or walk in town.

prep.title: Weather
prep.body: Pre-dawn trips are cold at 2,045 m. In the monsoon, landslides often disrupt roads and the railway.

faqs.q: How early is the Tiger Hill sunrise trip?
faqs.a: Leave around 3:30 am in season to reach the viewpoint before dawn.

faqs.q: Do I need to ride the whole toy-train line?
faqs.a: No. The full line from New Jalpaiguri is slow (20–25 km/h); a ride to Ghum and Batasia Loop gives the highlights.
On clear mornings, Everest and Kanchenjunga are both visible from Tiger Hill.
